alignments.note: Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else (rule 32); the participle carries the relativizer. Medium with the paired theos unit: the alternative reading that gives this article 'he is' moves the supplied copula off the predicate, so one decision governs both units, as EPH.6.9 hedges both of its own.
Substantival article before a participle supplies the pronoun and nothing else (rule 32).
The participle carries the supplied relativizer as a helper (rules 7, 32).

The generic noun 'thing' expands the demonstrative and stays with it, headed on 'this' (rules 15, 17). 2CO.7.11 aligns the identical auto touto the same way unhedged, giving 'selfsame' to the intensive and 'this thing' to the demonstrative.

Rule 53: the clause is verbless and the supplied copula is the predicate's helper. The subject is a substantival article plus participle, which rules 32 and 90 allow the pronoun and nothing else, so nothing on the subject side is left to carry it; no article before a participle carries a supplied copula in the corpus's 154 such configurations, and EPH.6.9's ho -> 'he' with kyrios -> 'who is Master' is the nearest analogue. Rule 63 is not cited, its exception being scoped to a lexical-noun subject. Medium because rule 92's reading of that scope leaves 'he is' on the article defensible.
Substantival article before a participle with one English word takes that relativizer (rule 90).
The case preposition rides with the pronoun, no article standing to anchor it (rules 21, 36).
'of the' is one unit on the article, headed on 'the' (rule 21).
